neighbours.label: A rate, speed or amount noun as the head of a prepositional phrase that quantifies how fast or how much ('at an alarming rate', 'in amounts of', 'at speeds over'), not the same noun as a plain subject or object
fire: The glaciers in the valley are melting at a startling rate this decade.
Arsenic was found in the well water in amounts well above the legal limit.
The jets flew over the base at speeds close to the sound barrier.
El hielo se derrite a una velocidad nunca vista en la región.
Women in the region are diagnosed at much higher rates than men.
Prices in the city have climbed at a steady pace since the spring.
The bacteria multiply at an astonishing speed in warm milk.
Lead turned up in the paint in quantities that alarmed the inspectors.
quiet: The exchange rate was published in the morning paper.
Speed matters less than accuracy in this kind of work.
The amount on the receipt did not match the bill.
La velocidad del tren nuevo sorprendió a los pasajeros.
Their pace was slow because the path was muddy.
The inspectors wrote down the quantity printed on each label.
She asked the bank to explain the new rates on her account.
The coach praised his speed after the match on Saturday.

predictions: Fire 0.40-0.90 on the rate/speed/amount noun; the same nouns as subjects or objects below 0.10.
notes: Card: ' rate', ' amounts', ' speed', ' velocidad', ' rates' inside 'at/in/with the X'. Probe: 'at an alarming rate' 0.411, 'in amounts of' 0.836, 'at speeds over' 0.777, 'a una velocidad alarmante' 0.912, 'at disproportionate rates' 0.596, 'at an alarming pace' 0.340 (synonym also fires); 'The interest rate was announced' 0.017, 'Speed is the main selling point' 0.009.
